summary: Checks whether a value is a scalar.
description: A primitive that carries a single value: string, number, boolean, symbol or bigint. `null` and `undefined` are primitives too, but they carry no value and do not qualify.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).
returns: `true` when the value is a scalar; otherwise `false`.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
isScalar("abc"); // => true
isScalar(1); // => true
isScalar(true); // => true
isScalar(10n); // => true
isScalar({}); // => false
isScalar([]); // => false
isScalar(null); // => false
```
